_README: Hand adjudication of the orphan clusters cbnf_yield.py finds: consolidated-report clusters that
no sub-agent flagged in the same run. An orphan is only a CANDIDATE promotion — the orchestrator
can also synthesize a finding across agents, and extraction can miss a sub-agent finding. Deciding
which is which requires reading the cluster against that run's actual CBNF bullets.
A token-containment score was tried as the decision rule and rejected: at the 0.5 threshold it
identified 2 of the 7 real promotions, and lowering it to 0.3 admitted two non-promotions while
still missing two real ones. The score tracks vocabulary overlap, not claim identity — a reviewer
dismissing X in prose about X scores the same as one dismissing Y in prose about X.
promotion: true  = the consolidated report carries a claim a sub-agent had explicitly dismissed.
promotion: false = no CBNF bullet in that run makes the claim; orchestrator-originated, or the
sub-agent finding was lost in extraction.
not computed results — the borderline ones say so in `note`.
